events.title: The Gunpowder Plot Foiled
events.description: Guy Fawkes was arrested beneath the House of Lords while guarding barrels of gunpowder intended to blow up Parliament and King James I during its State Opening. The plot was organized by a group of English Catholic conspirators led by Robert Catesby.
events.significance: The failed plot led to harsher anti-Catholic legislation in England and is commemorated annually as Guy Fawkes Night or Bonfire Night with fireworks and bonfires.

events.title: William of Orange Lands at Torbay
events.description: William of Orange landed in Devon, England, with a Dutch fleet and army, at the invitation of English political leaders opposed to the Catholic King James II.
events.significance: This event launched the Glorious Revolution, which deposed James II, established parliamentary supremacy, and led to the English Bill of Rights in 1689.

events.title: Woodrow Wilson Elected President
events.description: Democrat Woodrow Wilson won the U.S. presidential election, defeating incumbent William Howard Taft and former president Theodore Roosevelt, who ran on the Progressive Party ticket and split the Republican vote.
events.significance: Wilson's presidency brought major reforms such as the Federal Reserve Act and led the United States through World War I.

events.title: Monopoly Board Game Released by Parker Brothers
events.description: Parker Brothers began marketing Monopoly, a real estate trading board game based on earlier games such as The Landlord's Game, with Charles Darrow credited as inventor.
events.significance: Monopoly became one of the best-selling board games in history, sold worldwide in dozens of languages and editions.

events.title: Assassination of Rabbi Meir Kahane
events.description: Meir Kahane, the founder of the Jewish Defense League and the Israeli Kach party, was assassinated in New York City by El Sayyid Nosair after giving a speech at a hotel.
events.significance: Nosair's later links to the 1993 World Trade Center bombing connected the case to early developments in modern terrorism investigations in the United States.
